endorsements.quote: To address this, procurement frameworks may need to include mechanisms for independent validation and verification.

Procurement decisions must not only verify regulatory conformity but also critically assess whether the AI system is designed and validated to perform effectively in the intended clinical con text; quality is not just a matter of legal compliance, but of ensuring that the technology aligns with the realities of care delivery and makes a meaningful contribution to patient outcomes.
This could involve requirements for access to relevant technical documentation, audit rights, and the possibility of third-party evaluation or benchmarking against external standards.

To avoid financial waste, patient-safety incidents, and legal exposure, AI procurements should require local validation, ongoing monitoring of fairness and safety, and enforceable update and corrective-action obligations.

This may include multidisciplinary evaluation teams that combine clinical, technical, legal, and procurement expertise; clearer allocation of responsibility between suppliers and healthcare providers; and the use of external validation or auditing mechanisms where internal capacity is limited.

These elements can be embedded as minimum technical specifi cations, rewarded in award criteria when thresholds are exceeded or transparency is superior, and monitored through contract performance conditions with defined reporting cadences, drift triggers, and corrective-action timelines, using the levers provided by the legislation.

unlisted_practices: Require AI vendors to demonstrate clinical evidence of relevance and performance, preferably from appropriate clinical studies including randomised controlled trials where relevant.

Specify quality criteria in procurement technical specifications, award criteria and contract performance conditions, including both process measures (e.g., AI-literacy completion) and performance measures (e.g., diagnostic accuracy versus a local baseline and subgroup bias gaps).
Involve patients, the public and healthcare professionals in AI governance and procurement, including opportunities for their input and transparency on system performance and intended use.
Collaborate across regions or healthcare systems to share expertise and standardise AI evaluation approaches.

screen.reason: This is a legal and policy framework/commentary paper proposing procurement mechanisms and regulatory requirements for health care organizations adopting AI.
